# The soroauth C ABI

The signing core as a C shared library (`libsoroauth.so` / `libsoroauth.dylib`),
for language bindings. `@soroauth/node` is the first consumer.

```sh
# Build for the host platform (needs a C toolchain; cgo)
./build.sh /tmp/soroauth-c
# wrote /tmp/soroauth-c/libsoroauth.so
# wrote /tmp/soroauth-c/libsoroauth.h (generated by cgo)
```

The library is build output, never committed (`bindings/node/scripts/build.mjs`
stages its own copy). `soroauth.go` carries a `//go:build ignore` tag because
`c-shared` needs a C toolchain for its target, which the repository's
cross-compile matrix does not have; naming the file explicitly, as `build.sh`
does, compiles it anyway.

## Why it is string-based JSON

Every function takes UTF-8 C strings, returns a heap-allocated UTF-8 JSON
envelope, and the caller releases it with `SoroauthFree`:

```json
{ "ok": true,  "preimageXdr": "…", "payloadHex": "…" }
{ "ok": false, "error": "soroauth: preimage: source-account credentials …", "kind": "SOURCE_ACCOUNT_CREDENTIALS" }
```

JSON rather than a packed struct keeps the ABI stable as the library grows — a
new field is an added key, not a new calling convention — and it keeps the
policy in one place. `kind` is the Go sentinel the failure wraps, so a binding
can raise a typed exception (`MissingSigner`, `AlreadySigned`,
`TooManySignatures`, …) instead of string-matching a message; it is `ERROR` when
the failure was not one of the exported sentinels, which is what a malformed XDR
blob is. A binding that flattened all of those into one error would throw away
facts its callers need.

Nothing here decides anything: each function decodes its input, calls the same
`github.com/soroauth/soroauth-go` code the CLI and the wasm module call, and
encodes the result. That is what makes the golden-vector replay in
`bindings/node/test` meaningful — there is no second implementation of the
signing logic to disagree with the first.

## Functions

| Symbol                       | Purpose                                                         |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SoroauthVersion`            | The ABI version string, e.g. `soroauth-c-0.1.0`                 |
| `SoroauthPreimage`           | `HashIdPreimage` + payload for an address entry                 |
| `SoroauthPayload`            | Payload of an already-built preimage                            |
| `SoroauthWriteSignature`     | Write an externally produced signature ScVal onto the nodes     |
| `SoroauthAuthorizeWithSeed`  | Sign with one 32-byte ed25519 seed                              |
| `SoroauthAuthorizeWithSeeds` | Sign with 1..20 seeds (`AccountMultiSigner` when more than one) |
| `SoroauthInspect`            | `EntryInfo` as JSON                                             |
| `SoroauthAnalyze`            | Risk findings as JSON                                           |
| `SoroauthRenderInvocations`  | The invocation tree, ASCII                                      |
| `SoroauthRenderTree`         | The credential/delegate tree, ASCII                             |
| `SoroauthFree`               | Release any string this library returned                        |

The multi-seed function exists so the multi-signature path is proved through the
binding rather than reimplemented in each language: `AccountMultiSigner` is a
Go-only signer shape (sorted strictly ascending by public key, capped at the
host's 20), and a binding that built that vector itself would be testing itself.
